description: Real-time MCU: ESP32-S3 + onboard QMI8658C 6-axis IMU
package: dev board, on the lid; CBL-MCU-RIBBON soldered to its pad rows
notes: Mounted low for acceleration sensitivity. 17 GPIO on its two pad rows (1-7, 33-40, 43, 44) and 12 used; CBL-MCU-RIBBON takes them to J-MCU. Native USB - verified, not a UART bridge - so USB MIDI works. 4MB flash, 2MB QUAD PSRAM, both on-package: the vendor schematic marks U66 = ESP32-S3FH4R2 [datasheets/mechanical/WAVESHARE-ESP32-S3-MATRIX-SCHEMATIC.pdf; F=in-package flash, H4=4MB, R2=2MB quad PSRAM from Espressif's ordering code, from memory], so GPIO33-37 are free - octal PSRAM would have taken them. The 8x8 matrix is the instrument's only display, under a window in the top face (ADR 0015) - measure idle draw at E1 to size the shared lighting budget

description: Conformal coating for the in-body boards
notes: Breathed into for hours behind 18 unsealed switch cutouts, interior 10-20K above ambient. MASK BOTH SENSOR PORTS FIRST - a sealed reference chamber gains ~5.2kPa when warm and the output clips at zero, looking like a dead sensor (ADR 0003). THE SENSOR IS SOLDERED TO THE BOARD AND COATED WITH IT: a sensor swap breaks the coating at its eight joints - re-mask both ports before touching it up

part: 2-layer PCB - the main board: thumb switches, both thumb registers and the carrier circuits
description: Thumb switches and their registers, breath sensor, reference, ADC, umbilical, SPI egress, LED-strip drive and strip, the regulator, service header
package: long and narrow, sized in mechanical/drc.echo (main board), 1.6mm
notes: ONE board at the thumb level, mouth cap to the end of the right hand (ADR 0017). The thumb switches solder into it; the key boards connect to it by 12-way flat flex ribbons, a ZIF connector for each on its far edge. Parts face up - mechanical/drc.echo gives the room under the key boards and elsewhere. Holes over the U-bolt nuts, notches at the screws, standoffs off the oak or the thumb plates. Long: check the board house's panel and price before M4. Nothing on it is fast or RF - 2 layers, hand-assembled

description: The Matrix's connector on the main board: CBL-MCU-RIBBON plugs in here and unplugs when the lid comes off
notes: WHERE: the main board's tail end beside the regulator block, side entry, the ribbon arriving level from the mouth side; the LED strip stops short of it (mechanical/DESIGN.md). PINOUT: the 12 U-MCU-RT GPIO the instrument uses, 5V, 3V3 and GND are fixed by hardware/carrier/netlist.yaml; the other five positions are OPEN with CBL-MCU-RIBBON's conductor allocation. Under option (b) (CBL-MCU-RIBBON), put a ground between SCLK (IO35) and the chain clock (IO38); under (a) there is none to put there - the Matrix's only GND pad is on the other pad row. KEYED AND SHROUDED: a reversed plug puts 5V on a GPIO. RATING: the 5V and GND contacts carry the whole Matrix draw, and fed from the 5V pad nothing on the Matrix limits it (its USB diode is bypassed - matrix-led-current, power_path), so rate them against U-BUCK's 1A (R-78E5.0-1.0), not against matrix-led-current. A 1.27mm box-header contact is ~1A [from memory]: one 5V and one GND position would sit at the limit, so give some of the five open positions to extra 5V and GND - option (b) on CBL-MCU-RIBBON, the lean, still decided at M4/E11. PART NUMBER OPEN [from memory: 1.27mm dual-row box headers with a 0.635mm-ribbon IDC mate are a stock family; the envelope is from memory too]. Decided at M4 with the part in hand: the envelope, the latch and the mating IDC socket

part: 20-way flat ribbon, 0.635mm pitch, with a 2x10 1.27mm IDC socket at one end
description: The Matrix's wiring: soldered to its two pad rows on the lid, plugged into J-MCU on the main board
notes: CONDUCTORS: 20. Fixed: the 12 GPIO the instrument uses (hardware/carrier/netlist.yaml U-MCU-RT), 5V, 3V3 and GND. The Matrix's pad rows carry ONE GND pad [datasheets/mechanical/WAVESHARE-ESP32-S3-MATRIX-pinout.png: 5V GND 3V3 GP7-GP1 | GP33-GP40 TX RX]. The other five are OPEN: (a) the spare GPIO pads IO2-IO6 - spares reach the main board (ADR 0009's spare conductors), and ONE conductor carries the Matrix's 5V and ONE returns its LED current and every signal; or (b) extra 5V and GND - soldered to points on the Matrix off the pad rows (the vendor schematic's extension pads TP2 = VCC_5V, TP3 = GND [datasheets/MANIFEST.csv]), leaving no spares. THE LEAN IS (b), FOR CURRENT: rate the 5V and GND conductors against U-BUCK's 1A, not matrix-led-current (J-MCU row). A 0.635mm conductor carries 1A thermally [from memory] but its resistance is the problem: ~34mohm per 100mm [from memory, ~30AWG] is ~4 LSB full scale on the breath ADC per 100mA on one ground, ~40 at 1A, ~7 on six (carrier.md). What decides it: M4 with the board in hand (where a ground can be soldered), and E11 (breath output clean while the matrix is exercised): the Matrix's 3V3 is the ADC's reference (carrier/breath-adc) and is regulated against the Matrix's ground, so LED return current in the ribbon's ground moves that reference. BUILD: split the ribbon at the Matrix end into two halves, one per pad row; separate each conductor only as far as it travels to its pad, solder, then fix the ribbon to the board so it flexes behind the joints rather than at them [from memory]. Crimp the IDC socket with pin 1 marked. LENGTH: mechanical/drc.echo 'Matrix ribbon length' plus build slack - enough to lift the lid far enough to reach J-MCU. A DEAD MATRIX: unplug at J-MCU, lid off, desolder the ribbon from the pad rows and solder it (or a new one) to the replacement - a bench job, with no main-board rework
